correctness.rationale: The descent-flipping map swaps two singleton cycles with a transposition when the adjacent sites are mutually fixed or paired, otherwise conjugates by their adjacent-label transposition. It is an involution, preserves the complete remote fixed-site indicator vector and complements the adjacent descent. Conditioned counts of partner choices yield the two nonzero mixed covariance entries; the telephone recurrence proves the total and each interior sign. A ratio recurrence bounds T_{n-1}/T_n by 1/sqrt(n). Standalone exact enumeration passed 345599 checks through n=10 including every nonempty remote pattern. Universal claims are proved by the pairing/counting, not finite experiments.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Uniform involutions are a non-uniform conditioned subset of the symmetric group, so the full-permutation covariance matrix and its boundary cancellation cannot be restricted to obtain the involution matrix. The change from interior zero to strictly negative and limit −1 is an explicit implication-level separation. Conditional local fair descent after fixing all remote status coordinates is a separate stronger statement. The earlier fixed-transposition-class inversion formula dominates the aggregate covariance after mixing K; this corollary is not claimed original. It does not imply (1) or the labeled-site matrix (2) because K records only the total fixed-point number, not the remote fixed/nonfixed vector.

originality.rationale: Three independent searches of position-resolved involution/fixed-site/descent associations and primary literature full-text comparisons found no covering local pairing or entire remote fixed-status conditional-independence theorem. The strongest exact cycle-type/descent-set antecedent forgets fixed-point labels, while the nearest published sitewise covariance law assumes an entirely different permutation distribution; direct comparison of formulas disproves coverage. Priority is qualified by older general enumerators not fully readable. The earlier fixed-transposition-class inversion formula already implies aggregate covariance through mixing, so novelty is limited to fixed-location-resolved and full-vector conditional dependence.
residual_risks: The 1985 Désarménien–Foata original and the final 1993 Gessel–Reutenauer paper were not read in full; an unnoticed labeled-location refinement remains possible.

The self-review is not an independent priority certification.

value.rationale: The local descent complementing involution is a concrete dependence-preserving symmetry for arbitrary remote fixed-site configurations. It yields a full natural position-indexed covariance classification and a sharp structural contrast: interior fixed sites have negative covariance with descents in random involutions, though they cancel in uniform full permutations. It also identifies a nonvanishing limiting covariance −1, making the dependence law relevant for inference with random involution null models and prescribed fixed-point patterns, beyond a routine global moment recomputation. The aggregate covariance identity is a useful corollary but not a new independent contribution relative to earlier class-conditional descent probabilities.
